name: Contribution Margin Ratio
description: Calculate contribution margin as a percentage of price.
formula: Contribution margin ratio = (Price − Variable cost per unit) / Price
business_contexts: a manufacturer assessing what share of price covers fixed costs and profit
a subscription business assessing contribution margin ratio per plan
a retailer assessing contribution margin ratio across a product line
a food truck assessing contribution margin ratio per menu item
a hardware brand assessing contribution margin ratio per device
question_patterns: Given the price and variable cost per unit below, what is the contribution margin ratio?
Calculate the contribution margin ratio from the figures given.
What percentage of price is contribution margin, given the values below?
Calculate contribution margin as a ratio of price from the figures shown.
Using the price and variable cost given, what is the contribution margin ratio?
solution_logic: Step 1: Calculate contribution margin ratio = (price − variable_cost_per_unit) / price
key_insight: The contribution margin ratio turns a per-unit dollar margin into a percentage that scales across any volume — it answers 'how much of each sales dollar is left after variable cost.'
common_mistakes: Dividing by variable cost instead of price
Reporting the dollar contribution margin instead of converting it to a ratio
framework_soundbite: Contribution ratio is the per-unit margin expressed as a share of price, not a dollar figure.
